title: Free Draft-and-Verification: Toward Lossless Parallel Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
claim: Each forward pass both verifies the previous step's drafts and yields the logits for the next drafts, so decoding runs in a self-verifying parallel loop with no extra passes.
layout: 3 stages left-to-right, dashed red feedback loops, legend panel at left
description: A wide cream-colored figure split into two rounded panels. The left panel, labeled t=1, shows a column of gray masked tokens going into an orange DLLM block and coming out as blue predicted tokens. A legend below defines gray as Masked, blue as Predicted and green as Unmasked. The right panel, labeled 0<t<1, continues the flow. A green Remasking Scheduler turns the predictions into several candidate token columns marked with green check marks and a red X. These candidates go through a second DLLM and produce a new set of columns, with one column circled in red. A second Remasking Scheduler produces the next drafts. Dashed red arrows labeled 'indexing' and 'max_matched=2' loop back to the earlier stages. Solid arrows mean a model call and dashed arrows mean no model call. The eye goes first to the colorful token columns and the red feedback loops.
caption: The overview of FreeDave decoding. At the current step, the dLLM outputs the estimated distribution of the sequence, from which the remasking scheduler constructs multiple draft candidates. At the subsequent step, the same dLLM processes these candidates in parallel, verifying their validity via sequence matching. Then the resulting output distributions are reused to sample the next set of drafts. Because the logits needed for future drafts are naturally produced as byproducts of the verification step, FreeDave creates a continuous, self-verifying parallel decoding loop that requires no auxiliary models or extra forward passes.
abstract: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) have emerged as a compelling paradigm for language modeling, offering the unique potential for highly efficient inference via multi-token parallel decoding. However, unlocking this potential remains challenging. High-quality generation typically defaults to one-token-per-step static decoding, while existing parallel algorithms rely on heuristic confidence thresholds, introducing a fragile trade-off between decoding efficiency and generation quality. To overcome this, we introduce Free Draft-and-Verification (FreeDave), a novel training-free and model-free fast decoding algorithm. FreeDave capitalizes on the inherent properties of dLLMs by treating future token predictions as ``free drafts'' and rigorously self-verifying them in subsequent forward passes. Theoretically, FreeDave searches for a shorter decoding path that is guaranteed to reproduce the exact sequence generated by static decoding, achieving algorithmically lossless acceleration. With a sufficiently large draft budget and a verification frontier that does not retreat, it can use the fewest possible model forward passes among feasible paths. Extensive evaluations on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks demonstrate that FreeDave can boost the number of generated tokens per model forward (TPF) by up to 5.48$\times$ and tokens per second (TPS) by up to 3.94$\times$, while robustly maintaining generation quality and avoiding the task-specific performance degradation faced by heuristic methods. Code is available at https://github.com/cychomatica/FreeDave.
